error_context:
The CI run failed primarily because the async callback test suite (Run Background & Async Callback Tests on Python 3.9) experienced many test failures: server-side Dash/Flask raised an exception whenever a coroutine callback was invoked because the optional async extras were not available or async support was disabled. Evidence: repeated server logs "Exception: You are trying to use a coroutine without dash[async]. Please install the dependencies via `pip install dash[async]`..." coming from dash/backends/_flask.py:216, which produced HTTP 500 responses on POST /_dash-update-component and caused Selenium-based waits to time out (selenium TimeoutException: "text -> ... not found within 10s/15s"). These timeouts are visible in dash/testing/browser.py and selenium webdriver wait traces (WebDriverWait.until -> TimeoutException).

Secondary, the background-callback tests produced recurring "Address already in use" port-bind warnings for specific tests (e.g., tests/background_callback/test_basic_long_callback013.py / tests.background_callback.app_unordered) — the harness retried on another port and those tests eventually passed, so these were warnings, not the primary cause of the CI failure. Evidence: "Address already in use" and subsequent "Dash is running on http://127.0.0.1:58073/" followed by PASSED.

Additional failures/errors in other steps: the typing tests job reported a typing-related error (log message: "Values must be separated by a comma") which caused the Typing Tests step to fail. The Python 3.12 matrix run also reported a decoding/parsing error ("Can not decode value starting with character ')'"), indicating a separate failure in that matrix row. These errors are distinct from the async test failure but contributed to the overall failed run.

In short: (1) async tests failed because the Dash server refused to run coroutine callbacks due to missing/disabled dash[async], producing 500s and client-side timeouts (major root cause); (2) background tests showed port-binding collisions handled by retries (warning-level); (3) typing tests and the Python 3.12 matrix row had independent errors (typing/decoding) that also caused step failures.
